transcript.text: Hi, our integrated fridge freezer (behind a kitchen door) - the fridge is around 10 degrees but the freezer seems ok. We had a power cut a week ago, not sure if related. Rented flat, can't really take it out.

A warm fridge with a cold freezer usually points to an airflow issue rather than a lack of cooling power. The most common causes are simple: either the temperature setting was changed or left on a special mode, or something is blocking the vent at the back of the fridge that lets cold air in from the freezer. It could also be a fan inside the freezer that isn't pushing that cold air through.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
Thanks. The dial inside is on 3 out of 5, I haven't touched it. No burning smell or tripping, it's just running a lot. What should I check first?

Since the dial is set correctly and the freezer is still cold, the cooling system itself is likely working fine. The issue is probably that cold air isn't reaching the fridge compartment. This is most commonly caused by a blocked vent (often at the back of the fridge section) or an over-packed shelf stopping airflow. It could also be that the fan inside the freezer, which pushes this cold air through, has failed. Please check the back wall of the fridge compartment first. Is there any ice buildup visible, or is food/containers blocking the vent where cold air enters from the freezer?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I can't see any vent at the back of the fridge part, so not sure where it would be. There's some frost on the back of the freezer but not loads. Nothing is blocking anything in the fridge as far as I can tell.

This points strongly to a defrost system fault. In many integrated models, the evaporator (the cooling coils) is hidden behind the back panel of the freezer, so you won't see the ice directly from the fridge side. The cold air passes through a channel that can get blocked by ice if the defrost heater or thermostat fails. To check this safely: please switch the appliance off at the socket and leave both doors open for 24 hours to let all internal ice melt completely. After it has dried, plug it back in. If the fridge cools down normally but warms up again after a few days with frost returning, that suggests a failed defrost component (heater or thermostat) which will need an engineer to replace.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I can do that, but I'd have to empty everything out of both the fridge and freezer first. Is it definitely worth doing before reporting it to the letting agent? It's a rented flat so I can't open anything up or pull it out.

Yes, it is most likely worth doing. A full manual defrost is the standard first step for this symptom and will tell you if the problem is temporary ice blockage or a permanent fault. Since you are renting, please empty both compartments into cool bags with ice packs, place thick towels on the floor to catch melting water, switch the appliance off at the wall socket, and leave both doors open for 24 hours. Once completely dry, plug it back in and check if the fridge cools down again over the next few days. If it works but warms up later with frost returning, you have a failed defrost component (heater or thermostat) which requires an engineer to fix; report this result to your letting agent.
